answers.q1: Cargo (Rust, edition 2024, MSRV 1.96). Install dependencies with: cargo fetch --locked. Cargo has no separate install step, so `cargo build --workspace` also fetches them.
answers.q2: CI runs the full suite as `cargo test --verbose --workspace --features unstable-index`, then `cargo test --verbose --workspace --features pcre2`. The minimal form is: cargo test --workspace
answers.q3: cargo test --test it regression. The tests/tests.rs file declares `mod regression;` inside the `it` integration-test target (`[[test]] name = "it"` in Cargo.toml, autotests = false), so regression.rs is not a standalone target. Filtering by 'regression' selects its tests.
answers.q4: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings. CI's rustfmt job runs these two commands. It also runs docs: RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items --workspace
answers.q5: Cargo.lock and fuzz/Cargo.lock (lockfiles, per AGENTS.md). Also the build output in target/ and the git-ignored /deployment (man page and shell completions generated by build.rs). HomebrewFormula is only a symlink to pkg/brew. I found no vendored dependency directories.

q1.reason: Names Cargo, gives `cargo fetch --locked` (a cargo fetch variant), and notes cargo build fetches dependencies automatically.

q2.reason: Gives the CI `cargo test --verbose --workspace` form (plus pcre2) and the minimal `cargo test --workspace`; the extra unstable-index feature is harmless extra detail.

q3.reason: `cargo test --test it regression` matches the accepted command and correctly explains the `it` target.

q4.reason: Gives both `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, plus the cargo doc check as a bonus.

q5.reason: Lists Cargo.lock (and fuzz/Cargo.lock) and target/, which matches the accepted answer; it does not claim crates/*, tests/data or pkg/ are generated or vendored, and the build-generated /deployment is git-ignored output.
